heroLead: Slow, supportive 1:1 sessions of gentle movement and balance work — with seated and chair-supported options, built around your body and your pace. Practised alongside the care your doctor provides.
empathyLabel: You don't have to do this alone
empathyText: Staying steady on your feet matters. Yoga can be a gentle, supportive part of your week — building everyday mobility and confidence at a pace that suits you.
helpsH2: How yoga can support older adults.
helpsSubhead: Four gentle levers, working together — and the first one does most of the lifting.

levers.title: Everyday mobility
levers.body: Gentle movement helps joints feel easier for daily tasks.

levers.title: Better balance
levers.body: Supported balance work helps you feel steadier and more confident.

levers.title: Strength for daily life
levers.body: Gentle strengthening supports getting up, walking, and reaching.

levers.title: Calm and connection
levers.body: Breathing and relaxation for restful, settled days.

posesH2: The poses we focus on, and why.
posesSubhead: Grouped by what they do for the body. Your teacher draws from these — they won't ask you to do all of them.

poseGroups.why: Safe, accessible movement from a chair.

poses.desc: Gentle spinal mobility, eased from a chair to keep the back moving comfortably.
Easing the back with a soft, supported twist through the midsection.
Keeping the legs working with gentle circles and lifts from a seated position.
Calm and centring — a comfortable seat for soft, even breathing.

poseGroups.why: Balance and strength, always near a chair or wall.

poses.desc: Grounding and posture, with a chair within reach for steadiness.
Fingertips on a chair for support as you build gentle, steady balance.
Steady strength for the legs, holding a chair or wall for support.
Strength for getting up, practised slowly with the chair right behind you.

poseGroups.note: Standing balance work is always within reach of a chair or wall, and we move slowly between positions to avoid dizziness.

poses.desc: Loosening the upper body with slow, comfortable rolls and circles.
Everyday joint care to keep wrists and ankles moving with ease.
Opening the chest with a small, supported lift — no strain.

poseGroups.note: If you have osteoporosis or low bone density, we avoid deep forward bends and strong twists — please tell your teacher.

poses.desc: Soft and even breathing to settle the body and quiet the mind.
A soothing, low exhale that helps unwind tension.
On a chair or floor, as comfortable — a still close to every session.

selectionNote: Your teacher won't hand you all of these. They'll choose the right few for your body, your level, and how you're feeling that day.
howH2: How we work with you to get there.
howSubhead: One teacher who knows your name and your goals — not a different face every week.

steps.title: We get to know you
steps.body: A relaxed first session: your mobility, balance, any conditions, and what your doctor advises.

steps.title: A plan shaped to you
steps.body: Your teacher chooses seated, supported, or standing options to suit you.

steps.title: Guided live 1:1s
steps.body: The same teacher every time, on Google Meet, moving slowly and clearly.

steps.title: We grow it gently
steps.body: Small, steady progress toward easier, more confident movement.

whoForText: Older adults who want a safe, gentle, supportive practice for everyday movement and confidence.
testimonialQuote: At 72 I was nervous about starting. My teacher kept a chair beside me the whole time and went at my pace. I feel steadier on my feet and far more confident.

faqs.q: I haven't exercised in years, or I use a chair — can I still do this?
faqs.a: Yes. Sessions can be done seated or with chair support, and we start very gently and slowly.

faqs.q: I get dizzy or have trouble with balance — is it safe?
faqs.a: We move slowly, keep support within reach, and adapt to you. Please tell your teacher and check with your doctor first.

faqs.q: I have arthritis, or a knee or hip replacement — can I join?
faqs.a: Often yes, gently and adapted. Tell your teacher and check with your doctor first so we can plan around it.
We avoid deep forward bends and strong twists and keep movement safe and gentle. Please let your teacher know.

faqs.q: How soon might I notice anything?
faqs.a: Everyone is different. Many people feel a little steadier and more confident within a few weeks of gentle, regular practice.

safetyTitle: Yoga supports your care — it doesn't replace it
safetyText: These sessions support your overall wellbeing and are practised alongside professional medical care. They are not a substitute for diagnosis, treatment, or medication. Please tell your teacher about any conditions or symptoms so they can adapt your session safely, and keep your doctor in the loop.
metaDescription: Slow, supportive 1:1 yoga for older adults — gentle movement, balance, and chair-supported options to help with everyday mobility and confidence. First session free.
